name: Taiwan
summary_text: Taiwan is a progressive Asian destination — it was the first in Asia to legalise same-sex marriage (2019), the government is investing US$8.76 million to double gender-neutral public bathrooms by 2029, and a trans march in Taipei drew 3,000 participants in 2025. There are no documented severe incidents (no mob violence, trans-tourist rape, or organised dating-app predation). The main gaps are legal-gender-recognition reform stagnation — a 2008 Ministry order still requires sex-reassignment surgery to change one's gender marker (blocking an estimated 90% of trans people, with only case-by-case court exceptions), and the government has been "floundering" on reform — and a rising anti-gender discourse movement that has produced online waves of hostility. A trans woman was outed during a police identity inspection (the Viva case), and Taipei has held a vigil for victims of anti-trans violence. For a visitor, bathrooms are unrestricted (and being proactively expanded to gender-neutral), there is no criminalisation, and border/immigration poses no trans-specific friction. Taipei City has trans-friendly service guidelines.

sources.title: What About Trans Rights? Taiwan’s Ongoing Struggle for Self-ID – Taiwan Insight
sources.claim_summary: Taiwan Insight (Feb 2026): 'What about trans rights? Taiwan's ongoing struggle for self-ID' - the 2008 executive order requiring sex-reassignment surgery to change legal gender blocks an estimated 90% of trans people from obtaining matching national ID; every ID-requiring aspect of daily life (clinics, airport security) becomes a potential site of distress and discrimination; the Ministry of Health and Welfare has recognised gender self-determination as a human right since 2013.

sources.title: Taiwanese Government Continues to Flounder on Transgender Rights in 2025 Amidst Continued Transphobia – Taiwan Insight
sources.claim_summary: Taiwan Insight (Jan 2026): the Taiwanese government continues to flounder on transgender rights in 2025 amidst continued transphobia - no tangible policy change on abolishing the surgery requirement or expanding assisted reproduction; pending conscription-criteria changes could actively harm trans people; anti-gender movement activity rising, with organisations supporting Trump's anti-trans policies and the Taiwan Solidarity Party calling for a 'two genders' position.

sources.title: Ministry to invest in gender-neutral bathrooms - Taipei Times
sources.claim_summary: Taipei Times (Aug 2024): the Ministry of Environment will invest NT$280 million over four years to double gender-neutral public bathrooms nationwide (623 to 1,246 by 2029); of trans and gender-neutral survey respondents reporting discrimination, 17% occurred in public restrooms or changing rooms.

sources.title: Most Taiwan all-gender restrooms do not meet standards: Rights group - Focus Taiwan
sources.claim_summary: Focus Taiwan (Nov 2025): 'Most Taiwan all-gender restrooms do not meet standards: Rights group' — an LGBTQ+ rights group finds only 5 of 149 government-listed all-gender toilets met the required standards, including clear all-gender signage.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 404 - page removed); the underlying page addressed Taiwan's transgender rights - laws, protections and gaps.

sources.title: Taiwan Sees Rise in Anti-Gender Discourse Online | New Bloom Magazine
sources.claim_summary: New Bloom (Nov 2024): analysis of the wave of anti-gender discourse in Taiwan - rising anti-gender movement activity and its political context.

sources.title: Taipei Court Denies Transgender ID Change Request – TaiwanPlus
sources.claim_summary: TaiwanPlus (Aug 2024): a Taipei court denied a transgender woman's request to change the gender marker on her government ID without requiring surgery or a psychological evaluation; the supporting rights group says they will likely appeal.

sources.title: Taiwan dispatch: Transgender March held in Taipei as rights debate continues - JURIST - News
sources.claim_summary: JURIST dispatch (Nov 2025): the 7th annual Taiwan Transgender March in Taipei drew an estimated 3,000 people despite rain, with international participants; calls for an end to discrimination against trans people as the rights debate continues.

Utopia Asia Taiwan travel and resources page: 'one of Asia's most progressive countries for LGBT rights, and certainly the most liberal of the Chinese diaspora'; notes Taiwan regularised adoption for same-sex parents on May 16, 2023; listings of organisations, bars, spas and venues across 12 cities.
